questions.title: Basic Expected Value from a Discrete Distribution Table

parts.text: The discrete random variable $X$ has probability distribution given by $P(X = 0) = 0.1$, $P(X = 1) = 0.3$, $P(X = 2) = 0.4$, and $P(X = 3) = 0.2$. Calculate $E(X)$.

questions.title: Expected Value with Signed Outcomes and Long-Run Total

parts.text: A game awards a net gain of $X$ dollars with probabilities $P(X = -2) = 0.5$, $P(X = 1) = 0.3$, and $P(X = 5) = 0.2$. Find $E(X)$ and estimate the total expected gain over 200 independent plays.

questions.title: Normalizing Quadratic Mass Function and Calculating Expectation

parts.text: The discrete random variable $X$ takes values $-1, 1, 3$ with $P(X = x) = kx^2$. Find the value of $k$ and hence find $E(X)$.

questions.title: Machine Output Shift and 50-Day Cumulative Expectation

parts.text: A machine's daily output adjustment $X$ takes values $-2, 0, 1, 4$ with probabilities $0.1, 0.3, 0.2, 0.4$ respectively. Find $E(X)$ and hence determine the expected total output adjustment over 50 days.

questions.title: Expected Value of a Fair 6-Sided Die

parts.text: A fair 6-sided die is rolled once. Let $X$ be the number shown on the upper face. Find $E(X)$ and explain why $E(X)$ need not be an attainable value of $X$.
A discrete random variable $X$ takes values 1, 2, 4 with probabilities $\frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{3}, \frac{1}{6}$ respectively. Calculate $E(X)$ as an exact fraction in simplest form.

questions.title: Drawing Counters Without Replacement and Calculating Mean

parts.text: A bag contains 6 yellow counters and 4 green counters. Two counters are chosen at random without replacement. Let $X$ be the number of yellow counters chosen. Draw up the probability distribution table for $X$.
Calculate $E(X)$.

questions.title: Finding Unknown Parameter and Expected Total over Repeated Trials

parts.text: The discrete random variable $X$ takes values $-3, 0, 2, 5$ with probabilities $0.2, 0.3, p, 0.1$ respectively. Find the value of $p$.
Calculate $E(X)$, and find the expected total score after 150 independent trials of $X$.

questions.title: Two-Attempt Stopping Game Model and Long-Run Profitability

parts.text: A player is allowed at most two attempts in a game. The probability of success on each independent attempt is 0.4. Success on the first attempt gives a net gain of 2 dollars, success on the second attempt gives a net gain of 0.5 dollars, and failure on both attempts gives a net loss of 1 dollar (represented as $-1$). The game stops after the first success or after two attempts. Let $X$ be the net gain in dollars. Draw up the probability distribution table for $X$.
Calculate $E(X)$ and explain whether playing this game is advantageous to the player in the long run.

questions.title: Minimum Score Game and Probability of Exceeding the Mean

parts.text: Two fair 4-sided dice, each numbered 1, 2, 3, 4, are thrown. The score $X$ is 0 if the two numbers match; otherwise $X$ is the smaller of the two numbers. Draw up the probability distribution table for $X$.
Calculate $E(X)$, and find $P(X > E(X))$.

questions.title: Cubic Probability Mass Function and Long-Run Observation Total

parts.text: The discrete random variable $X$ takes values 1, 2, 3, 4 only, with probability function $P(X = x) = cx^3$, where $c$ is a constant. Show that $c = \frac{1}{100}$ and draw up the probability distribution table for $X$.
Calculate $E(X)$, and find the expected sum of the scores in 80 independent observations of $X$.

questions.title: Hypergeometric Sampling Distribution and Expected Value Proof

parts.text: A box contains 3 red balls and 5 blue balls. Three balls are chosen at random without replacement. Let $X$ be the number of red balls chosen. State all possible values of $X$ and explain why $X$ cannot take the value 4.
Draw up the probability distribution table for $X$, giving each probability as an exact fraction in simplest form.
Calculate $E(X)$ and verify that it equals $n \times \frac{R}{N}$, where $n = 3$ is the sample size, $R = 3$ is the total number of red balls, and $N = 8$ is the total number of balls in the box.

questions.title: Carnival Coin Game: Net Gain Distribution, Expectation, and Fair Price

parts.text: At a carnival stall, a player pays 2 dollars to play a game. A bag contains 2 gold coins, 3 silver coins, and 5 bronze coins. The player draws 2 coins at random without replacement. Each gold coin pays 5 dollars, each silver coin pays 2 dollars, and bronze coins pay nothing. Let $X$ be the player's net gain in dollars (gross payout minus the 2 dollar fee). Draw up the probability distribution table for $X$.
Calculate $E(X)$.
During a weekend carnival, 500 games are played. Find the stall operator's expected total profit or loss, and state the fee the operator should charge per game to make the game fair.
